brief_name: Navreo VP/Head of Sales Hiring Signal

ideation.icp_description: B2B companies hiring a VP/Head of Sales or equivalent senior sales leader (CRO, CSO, VP Revenue, Head of Revenue). Buyer is the CEO/Founder running the search. Signals: CEO making a strategic move to scale outbound, new sales leader faces an immediate build-vs-buy decision on outbound infrastructure. Company size 11-200, in 14 high-GDP countries, direct employers (not recruiting agencies).
ideation.offer: Navreo outbound infra DFY, pay-per-lead. The new VP plugs into a working outbound system on day 1 instead of rebuilding from scratch in their first quarter. CEO de-risks the senior sales hire (no infra build cost, no pre-commit, performance basis).
why_signal_fits_angles: New VP Sales = ~$200K+ base salary investment. CEO has already committed to scaling sales. We make the hire's first 90 days productive instead of infrastructural.
Pay-per-lead removes budget pre-commit risk since the VP hasn't proven ROI yet.
Twin-buyer pitch: lands with the CEO ('de-risk your hire') AND with the incoming VP ('skip the 90-day infra build, start booking meetings week 2').

angles_tested.drop_reason_for_acronyms: Bare CRO/CSO acronyms dropped — collide with Chief Risk Officer, Chief Safety Officer, Conversion Rate Optimisation, Contract Research Organization. Full spellings only.

angles_tested.drop_reason: Director-level too noisy at the keyword level — catches Partnerships Sales, Regional Sales, Brand Partnership Sales, Geo-specific Sales (North America Data Center), Vertical Sales (Ocular Biologics). At title-keyword level there is no clean way to distinguish 'head of sales for the whole company' from 'director of [some specific region or segment]'.

ABORT — 'Commercial' is fatally overloaded. Sample hits: Commercial Finance, Commercial Marketing, Commercial Operations, Commercial Supply Chain, Commercial Performance Improvement, Commercial Energy Strategy, PA to Commercial Director. EU coverage loss is smaller than raw numbers suggest — Angle A already catches the German 'Head of Sales (d/w/m)' role.

Too low volume to be worth a separate angle. Bare 'Founding Sales' pulls in 'Founding SDR' / 'Founding BDR' (junior salespeople, not leaders). Founding/first-hire angle is still captured via lilly-theirstack-data-processing's per-lead HowWeCanHelp angle waterfall (Priority 1) when any role title from Angle A/B contains 'Founding' or 'First'.

qualification._purpose: Role-only judgement layer applied by lilly-theirstack-data-processing Phase 2.5. Classifies each new Jobs row as QUALIFIED / BORDERLINE / OFF_BRIEF based on whether the role signals 'CEO scaling outbound with a new senior sales leader who will OWN the motion'. Companies are NEVER excluded by this gate — only specific roles. A company hiring a regional sales manager today is still a fine prospect under a different brief tomorrow.
qualification.role_signal_definition: The new hire will OWN the company's outbound sales motion as a senior leader. Not a quota-carrying IC, not a field/regional/channel head, not a sales-ops or sales-enablement role. CEO/Founder is making a deliberate 'we're scaling outbound' investment.
qualified_role_patterns: VP of Sales / VP Sales / Vice President of Sales / Vice President Sales
Head of Sales / Head of Global Sales / Head of Sales & BD
Chief Revenue Officer / CRO (full spelling) — when title makes clear it's a revenue role
Chief Sales Officer / CSO (full spelling) — when title makes clear it's a sales role
Director of Sales / Senior Director of Sales (at 11-200 emp, IS the head-of equivalent)
VP of Revenue / VP Revenue / Head of Revenue
Head of Commercial / VP Commercial / Commercial Director (UK/EU phrasing — apply with caution given the Commercial keyword overload)
Head of New Business / Director of New Business (UK phrasing for outbound sales lead)
disqualified_role_patterns: Account Executive / AE / Senior AE / Enterprise AE — IC quota-carrier, not GTM leader
SDR / BDR / Sales Development Representative / Business Development Rep — execution layer
Sales Manager (regional / area / branch / district / territory) — field/team layer
Inside Sales Manager / Inside Sales Lead / Inside Sales Director — team-of-AEs manager
VP Sales Operations / Director of Sales Operations / Head of Sales Ops / RevOps — ops layer
Sales Enablement Manager / Director of Sales Enablement / Head of Enablement — enablement layer
VP Channel Sales / Head of Channel / Channel Sales Director / Partner Sales VP — partner motion
VP Partnerships / Head of Partnerships / BD Partnerships — partnerships, not outbound
VP Customer Success / Head of CS / Customer Success Manager — retention, not new-logo hunting
Solutions Engineer / Sales Engineer / VP Sales Engineering / Pre-Sales — technical pre-sales
Sales Trainer / Sales Coach — coaching role
Internal Sales / Telesales / Inbound Sales Rep — inbound order-taking
Wholesale Sales Manager / Distributor Sales / Dealer Sales / Trade Sales — channel/transactional ops
Retail Sales Manager / Field Sales Rep / Field Sales Manager — store/territory rep
Sales Recruiter / Sales Recruitment Manager / Talent Acquisition (Sales) — internal recruiter
VP Sales Strategy / Sales Strategy Director — strategy/planning role, not GTM owner
borderline_role_patterns: Director of Sales at 100-200 emp — could be true sales leader OR mid-layer reporting to existing VP
Head of GTM / VP GTM — could be sales-led (qualified) OR product/growth-led (less fit)
Director of Business Development at <50 emp — could be outbound sales leader OR partnerships-leaning
Regional VP Sales / VP Sales — North America / VP US Sales — geo-specific; usually disqualified at >100 emp
Senior Sales Manager at 11-30 emp — could be first true sales hire OR retitled senior IC AE
Sales Director (no prefix, ambiguous level) at 50-100 emp — mid-market UK phrasing

filter._expected_daily_volume: ~25 jobs/day post-negatives (raw ~26/day from Angles A+B combined, minus noise removed by negatives)

dm_finder._note: Buyer is the CEO/Founder running the search — NOT the incoming VP being hired (they don't exist yet, or if they do, the new one is being hired). Excludes COO/CFO since the sales hire is a CEO-led decision in 90%+ of cases.

personalization._note: Email copy is ground truth for what to personalise. Skill 2 reads the Smartlead campaign email body → identifies all {{merge_variables}} → looks up generation instructions in per_lead_variables below. Variables present in copy but missing here will halt the run. The 'ideation.offer' field above provides SENDER CONTEXT (what the sender does) which the LLM uses as background when generating per-lead values — it is NOT a Smartlead merge variable, it's not in the email body. Role.instructions: Direct field lookup WITH email-readability normalisation. Copy the Jobs row's 'Job Title' value, then normalise so it reads naturally after the hardcoded 'Saw you were hiring a ___' hook. Rules: (1) Replace ', ' separating a level word from a function area with ' of ' — e.g. 'Director, Revenue Operations' → 'Director of Revenue Operations'. (2) Drop bracketed/parenthetical text and reformulate if it changes the noun phrase. (3) Trim whitespace. (4) Preserve seniority words ('Senior', 'Director', 'Manager', 'Head', 'VP', 'Lead', 'Chief'). No LLM call needed for cases (1)-(3); only escalate to LLM if the title is genuinely ambiguous after rule-based normalisation. Inherits GTM brief's Role rule verbatim.
Role.validation: Non-empty. Must read naturally after 'Saw you were hiring a ___'. Must NOT contain commas in the level-word/function-area position. Must NOT contain parens. Preserves the semantic role from the joined Jobs row.

Icebreaker.instructions: Delegate to the lilly-icebreaker skill. CRITICAL: SKIP both the Hiring angle AND the 'You joined' (change-of-roles) angle for this brief. The entire campaign is already triggered by a hiring signal (referenced explicitly via {{Role}} in the email's hook), so duplicating the hiring angle in the Icebreaker would feel redundant. Change-of-roles is also excluded because referencing the DM's own recent role change compounds the personal-detective signal in a way that reads stalkerish when paired with the hiring-hook (rule set 2026-05-17 — applies to ALL hiring-signal briefs). Allowed angle waterfall for this brief: Colleague → Funding → Tech → Fallback. Pass the DM's company + title + LinkedIn URL to the skill, plus an explicit 'skip_angles: [Hiring, You joined]' instruction.
Icebreaker.validation: Non-empty. Must NOT reference 'hiring', 'open role', 'looking for', or any active-hiring language. Must NOT reference the DM's recent role change ('stepped into', 'took over', 'new in your seat', 'X years in role'). Per lilly-icebreaker's other validation rules.

HowWeCanHelp._note: Skill 2 evaluates triggers in priority order; first matching angle fires; if no specific angle matches, fallback (priority 99) always fires. Each angle produces a sentence-completion clause that drops into the email's 'wanted to reach out because ___' stem. CRITICAL: use 'they' to refer back to the role mentioned in the hook — do NOT repeat the role title in the because-clause (causes word repetition in the email's opening sentence).

angles.trigger: hiring_for (the Jobs row's Job Title) matches /(Founding|First)/i
angles.instructions: When the hire's title contains 'Founding' or 'First', the new sales leader has no existing outbound to inherit. Pitch: founding hires usually burn their first quarter on outbound setup (sender domains, sequences, list building), and we can hand them a working pipeline instead so they focus on the strategic build (team hiring, enablement, playbooks). Use the phrase 'founding hires' generically (not 'your new founding hire') to avoid repeating the role word from the hook. End with 'instead' (clean tail).
angles.example: founding hires usually lose their first quarter to outbound setup, and we can hand yours a working pipeline instead

angles.trigger: always (after Priority 1 founding/first check fails) — fires for every lead. Output branches based on company employee_count.
angles.instructions:
Two sub-branches based on employee_count:

1. SMALL-CO BRANCH (employee_count < 50): the new VP is probably the first true senior sales hire — CEO has been doing sales themselves, urgency is high, the new hire needs pipeline immediately. Pitch: they'll want to start booking pipeline immediately, we can fill their calendar by week 2 on a performance basis. Use 'they'll' to refer back to {{Role}} (already mentioned in the hook). Preserves user's 'want to' wording (set 2026-05-17, softer than 'need to').

2. LARGER-CO BRANCH (employee_count 50-200): there's usually an existing outbound function — maybe a previous VP left, maybe scaling past first VP. The new hire walks in to a partial system and faces 90 days of stabilising before they can ship new initiatives. Pitch: they'll spend their first 90 days stabilising the existing outbound motion, we can run that layer on a performance basis so they focus on strategy. Use 'they'll' to refer back to {{Role}}.

Default to LARGER-CO when employee_count is missing or ambiguous.

WORDING NOTE (set 2026-05-17): use 'performance basis' not 'pay-per-lead' — applies to all angles in this waterfall. 'Performance basis' is broader and matches the email body's existing pricing language.
angles.example_small_co: they'll want to start booking pipeline immediately, and we can fill their calendar by week 2 on a performance basis
angles.example_larger_co: they'll likely spend their first 90 days stabilising outbound, and we can run that layer on a performance basis so they focus on strategy

angles.trigger: always — fires when no priority 1-2 angle matches (rare; safety net)
angles.instructions: Clean generic that always works. Mentions a working pipeline + performance basis + booking meetings from day 1. Use 'they'd' to refer back to {{Role}}. Avoid repeating the role title. Trailing 'on a performance basis' is non-negotiable — it anchors to the brief's offer.
angles.example: with a working pipeline on a performance basis, they'd be booking meetings from day 1

HowWeCanHelp.validation: 14-25 words. Starts mid-sentence (lowercase, since 'because' precedes it). Follows the matched angle's instructions. Must NOT repeat the role title (use 'they' / 'they'll' / 'they'd' / 'yours' instead). Must NOT duplicate {{Cold Email Video Angle}}'s content (that variable handles the company-specific sales outcome later in the email). Must include 'performance basis' language for angles 2 and 3 (angle 1 is exempt — it ends with 'instead'). Do NOT use 'pay-per-lead' — wording rule set 2026-05-17.

Cold Email Video Angle.instructions:
Generate a one-line sentence-completion for the email stem 'I recorded a short-video for {{company_name}} showing a teaser of what we'd {build|set up} to ___'. The angle is PURE ICP-connection: how we'd help the company connect with their target buyers (their ICP). Reference what THE COMPANY's ICP looks like (e.g. for Fullbay → heavy-duty repair shops; Osmind → psychiatry practices; Canopy → accounting firms; Xelix → AP teams). Form: starts with an infinitive verb (drive / fill / open / build), references a sales outcome anchored to the company's specific ICP segment.

EXPLICITLY DO NOT INCLUDE:
- Commercial model language ('on a pay-per-result basis' / 'on a performance basis' / 'pay-per-lead' / 'guaranteed' etc.) — that's already covered in {{HowWeCanHelp}} earlier in the email. Including it here is redundant.
- The channel/method ('through outbound' / 'through cold outbound') — implied by the email being a cold outreach, not needed in the angle.
- The prospect's title or role — covered in the email's hook via {{Role}}.
- The company name — '{{company_name}}' already appears immediately before this slot in the template.

The angle should be PURE: company's ICP segment + a sales-outcome verb (drive demos / open accounts / fill pipeline). Nothing else.

OVERRIDE NOTE: This instruction OVERRIDES Navreo's global memory rule 'feedback_cold_email_angle_title_relevance' (which says the angle must reference the prospect's title) FOR THIS BRIEF ONLY. The prospect's title appears in the hook already, so the angle stays role-free.

MANDATORY: WebFetch the company's homepage BEFORE generating this angle. Industry tags alone are too coarse — must verify what the company actually does for ICP-segment accuracy.
Cold Email Video Angle.validation: 5-12 words, sentence-completion form (starts with infinitive 'drive' / 'fill' / 'open' / 'build' / etc., NOT a full sentence). Must reference the company's specific ICP segment (their target buyer type). Must NOT repeat the company name. Must NOT reference the prospect's title or role. Must NOT include commercial model language ('pay-per-lead' / 'performance basis' / 'guaranteed'). Must NOT include channel/method ('through outbound' / 'cold outbound') — keep it pure ICP-connection.

CaseStudy.instructions: Delegate to lilly-personalisation's bucketed CaseStudy generation. Match a case study to the DM's role/vertical/company-size bucket (Navreo's standard bucket scheme). The skill maintains the bucket → case-study mapping; this brief inherits Navreo's default mapping unless explicitly overridden.
CaseStudy.validation: Per lilly-personalisation's CaseStudy validation. Must include hard numbers (revenue, lead count, conversion lift, etc.) per Navreo's case-study convention.
